Subject: Quick Q: audit/access logs retention & export capabilities

Hi Soojin,

We're finalizing our control matrix for the upcoming vendor review and had two specific asks on logs:

1) What are the default retention windows you offer for (a) audit logs (admin actions/console/API-level) and (b) access logs (token usage, request-level telemetry) in the Hosted product?
2) Can customers export logs (audit + access) on-demand to customer-owned S3 / GCS with schema and retention preservation? Is there an automated scheduled export option?
3) If a customer requests deletion for a tenant (GDPR / data subject request), what is the deletion workflow for logs and how do you prove removal?

We're primarily interested in Hosted but curious about Dedicated/Private options too.

Appreciate a concise breakdown and any links to docs or templates we can attach to the control questionnaire.

Subject: Re: Quick Q: audit/access logs retention & export capabilities

Hi Dana — thanks for the clear asks. Below is a concise Q&A and the practical steps we recommend for your control matrix.

Summary (short):
- Hosted defaults: access logs = 90 days; audit (configuration/admin) logs = 365 days.
- Exports: Hosted supports both ad-hoc API exports and scheduled delivery to customer-owned S3 (NDJSON/CSV); Dedicated/Private can extend retention or keep logs in customer VPC.
- Deletion: We support tenant-level deletion requests. Hosted uses a coordinated soft-delete → purge pipeline with signed attestations and export logs to demonstrate completion; Private deployments can run local purge jobs per policy.

Detail:
1) Retention windows (Hosted):
  - Access logs (ingress/egress request traces, token-level): default 90 days; configurable up to 13 months for enterprise contracts.
  - Audit logs (console/admin/API changes, privilege changes, service-account activity): default 365 days; configurable up to 3 years for compliance plans.
  - Notes: retention can be set per-tenant in Dedicated and Private, subject to resource/contract limits.

2) Export capabilities:
  - On-demand exports: Console and Logs API provide ad-hoc exports (NDJSON or CSV) for both audit and access logs.
  - Scheduled exports: We offer scheduled delivery (daily/weekly) to customer-owned S3 buckets (AWS) or GCS buckets (via signed-transfer). Exports include a manifest + schema file and an integrity checksum (SHA256).
  - Formats & schema: audit logs use NDJSON with canonical fields (timestamp, actor_id, actor_ip, action, resource_type, before/after) ; access logs include request_id, model, token_counts, latency_ms, response_status. We attach a matrix with field mapping.
  - Immutable exports: For regulated customers we can configure WORM (write-once) export objects and signed manifests to satisfy retention and tamper-evidence requirements.

3) Deletion & erasure workflow (Hosted):
  - Step 1: Customer submits deletion request through Console or Support (specify tenant id and scope).
  - Step 2: We mark data as 'to-be-deleted' (logical/soft delete) and remove indexed access; we begin deletion of hot-store copies immediately.
  - Step 3: Background purge job deletes cold/archival copies within the configured purge window (default 30 days; can be shortened with contract terms).
  - Step 4: For auditability we provide a signed deletion attestation (timestamp, scope, operator id) and an export of the pre-deletion manifest showing objects removed.
  - Caveats: If logs have been exported to customer-owned buckets, Redwood cannot remove copies from those buckets; we document this exception in the attestation.

4) Demonstrating removal / evidence for auditors:
  - Signed deletion attestation (PDF) with job id and hashes.
  - Pre/post manifests showing object ids removed.
  - Audit trail entries (immutable) that show the deletion operation (operator, timestamp).

5) Private/Dedicated specifics:
  - Dedicated: We can increase retention SLA and route scheduled exports into your VPC-managed buckets. Deletion timelines are identical but performed under your tenancy control for on-prem storage.
  - Private (on-prem): You control the retention and purge windows; Redwood provides the tooling and a recommended purge playbook.

References & next steps:
- Export policy matrix attached: export-policy-matrix.pdf (maps fields & retention options).
- Console docs: https://console.redwood.ai/docs/logs#exports
- If you want, we can provision a scheduled export trial to your S3 for 7 days so your SOC team can inspect schema and manifests.

Action items:
- Dana: confirm whether you want a one-time export sample to your S3 or a 7-day scheduled trial.
- Neha: I will need the account/tenant id to generate the sample and the S3 bucket ARN if they choose trial.

Let me know if you'd like this condensed into a single control text snippet we can paste into your vendor questionnaire.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
